intent: "Can this account search now, and what is left?" — allowed or not, why not, and the credits and room the provider can say

input_schema.title: audience.availability input
input_schema.description: Whether the account the route binds may search the provider's database now. Nothing is named: the binding names the account.

args.description: Nothing: the account is the binding's.

external_ids.description: Only this plugin's own pins reach it. The answer names no campaign: what an account may do is the account's.

available.description: Whether a search by this account would be started now, as far as the provider can say before one is.

reason.description: Why not, where `available` is false: `no_credits`, the account's credits are spent; `not_permitted`, the user the plugin signs in as may not search, such as a member whose role is restricted; `not_included`, the account's plan does not include searching, or holds no more contacts; `other` for a reason this vocabulary has no word for. Null where `available` is true.

detail.description: The provider's own words for why not, as it gives them, or null where it gives none.

credits.description: What the account has to spend, where the provider can say; null where it cannot.

balance.description: The credits left, in the provider's own unit, or null where it does not say.

price_per_person.description: What one person found and taken costs, in the same unit, or null where it does not say.

currency.description: The unit both are counted in — `credits`, or a currency's code — or null where the provider does not say.

headroom.description: How many more people the account's plan lets it hold, or null where the provider does not say.

vendor.description: The provider's own word for the account's state. A closed list, so nothing else travels here.

failure_codes.when: The provider's answer was larger than this installation lets a plugin read from a program (`Plugins:Exec:OutputBytes`), so it was cut off; asking again would cut it the same way.
The vendor tool refused the call or never started, so nothing the operation asks for was ever attempted. Repeating it runs the same broken call.
The plugin's own credential does not let it read what this account may do. This code stands for an answer the plugin cannot read as a provider block; one it can is `provider_blocked`.
The provider refused the call for now and it may be attempted again.
The provider could not be reached, or answered with a failure on its own side.
The provider was called and no answer arrived. A read changes nothing, so the next attempt simply asks again.

The provider refused this call for a reason outside the work item — the account's money or plan, an allowance it counts, a credential it no longer accepts, a channel disconnected or paused — and did nothing for it. The failure's block says what is blocked, why and where a person clears it; a repeat once it clears is a first act. It is said even where the operation also declares an older code for the condition, which then stands for an answer the plugin cannot read as a block.

conformance: `available` is the provider's answer as far as it can give one before a search starts; a search may still be refused for a reason the provider only says then.
Where `available` is false, `reason` says why in this vocabulary and `detail` in the provider's own words; where it is true, `reason` is null.
A provider that can say nothing beyond whether the account may search answers `available` with `credits` and `headroom` null, never a number it does not know.
A user the plugin signs in as who may not search is `available: false` with `not_permitted`, an answer, not `unauthorized`, which says the credential cannot read even this.
A state this vocabulary has no word for is `other`, with the provider's own word under `vendor.status`.
